content.comment_body: For my application, I need the [product_name] to switch to RUN mode immediately upon being powered on. I've checked various manuals but couldn't find a solution. The program loads and works, with a main switch controlling ON/OFF. Ideally, the device should start running automatically at power-up instead of going to the menu. It seems like a straightforward requirement, but I'm unable to find the answer. Can anyone provide a link or resource explaining how to achieve this? Thanks.

Hello, You can refer to the manual for [product_name], specifically chapter 2.4. According to the manual, if there's a circuit program in the device or on the card, it will remember its operational state before power-off. Versions without a display unit automatically switch from STOP to RUN. Best regards, [user_name]
Switch your [product_name] to RUN mode. After that, whenever you power up the device, it will automatically enter RUN mode.

Dear [user_name], Normally, the [product_name] should remain in RUN mode after powering on if it was in RUN mode before shutting down. If you switch it off while in STOP mode, it will stay in STOP after power up. If this doesn't resolve the issue, I recommend downloading a simple program to check for potential problems. Also, verify if you're using an initialization flag (such as M8) in your program. Regards, [user_name]

Thanks everyone for your assistance. Something seems off somewhere! The program is present and working without obvious bugs. I'm using a [product_name] with transistor outputs and an analog module, both powered together via 24VDC. On initial power up, the device shows the regular menu and requires manual navigation to enter RUN mode. After running, if I power off and then on, it returns to the menu and requires manual intervention again. I'm not using the M8 flag. Is there another setting that might cause this issue? I can't share my program file since this site doesn't accept the required format. [user_name]

Is there a functioning program in your [product_name]? Also, ensure there's no memory card or any device connected, and that the PC cable is unplugged. Typically, if the device was running before power was lost, it should start automatically in RUN mode after power returns. Steps: load program, set to RUN, verify operation. When powered down, the device stops, and when power is restored, it should resume running automatically.

Hello [user_name], Thank you for your reply. Yes, the program is loaded and runs without errors. There's no memory card or cable connected. I understand that the device should resume running automatically after a power cycle if it was running before. However, mine doesn't do this, hence my request for help. Perhaps there's a subtle issue or configuration in the program, possibly related to a flag like M8 (though I’m not using it). In summary, the program runs only when started manually after each power-up. If anyone can review my program, I'm happy to share it, but I can't upload it directly here. Thank you.
Hello [user_name], Did you try testing with a very simple program, only using the basic module without any extra cards? You can compress your program and attach it here. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], Thank you for following up and suggesting to zip the program. I no longer have the system, so I can't easily test by removing the extra analog module. During earlier development, the device would auto-run as expected, but at some point it stopped. Changes made during development likely contributed, but the exact transition isn't clear. Initially, the analog outputs were not included until the module arrived, so the auto-run worked without the module. All this suggests the issue may be in the program itself. If you can review my program, I'd appreciate it and don't mind any feedback. Many thanks,

It seems your [product_name] may be malfunctioning. Try using a different device. Any functioning [product_name] should restart automatically in RUN mode after a power failure if it was running before. If it doesn’t, your device might be defective.

Hello [user_name], I tested your program on [product_name] and there were no issues. The device restarts in RUN mode after a power failure, so it’s likely a hardware problem — possibly with the basic module or the extension module. Try running your program only with the basic module. Best regards, [user_name]

Dear [user_name], Thanks for your feedback! It seems your system may indeed have a fault, possibly as the analog module was added. I will ask the user to disconnect the analog module and run the program as is to see what happens. I'll keep you updated. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello, I have results from further tests. Following [user_name]'s suggestion, I removed the analog module, but the [product_name] still didn’t auto-start in RUN mode after power cycling. I also tried the same program on another [product_name] (230V version), which worked as expected after power loss. I’ve sent the problematic device to [company_name] for repair or replacement. Still, I wonder if some internal setting or bit could cause this behavior, since everything else works fine. Thank you all for your assistance.
Hello [user_name], There is likely no internal setting causing this. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users expect the [product_name] device to automatically resume RUN mode after a power cycle if it was active prior to shutdown. In this case, the user's device repeatedly returns to the start menu and requires manual intervention to launch RUN mode after each power-up. This contrasts with both the documentation and feedback from other users, highlighting confusion and potential inefficiencies due to the discrepancy between expected and actual behavior.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants the [product_name] to automatically resume RUN mode after each power cycle, without requiring manual action, consistent with documented behavior and typical community practices.
